Each frame is 258 bytes: 0xFE + 256 payload bytes (one per channel) + 0xFD. The 25 µs carrier (载波) at 40 kHz is split into 16 phase bins of 1.5625 µs; 256 PhaseLine instances output high between on-step and off-step, so the width is (off − on) mod 16 bins and the fundamental amplitude (基波幅度) follows sin(π·width/16), maximum at 8 bins, i.e. 50 % duty (占空比). A full-width pulse starts at phase+1 and ends at phase+9, centred on phase+5. Narrowing the pulse without moving the start would shift that centre, so an amplitude change would drag the phase and pull the beam. The RTL therefore shifts on-step later by lead = 4 − width/2, keeping every width centred on phase+5: amplitude changes leave the phase untouched.

Bits 7–4 of each byte are the amplitude code (幅度码) 0–15 and bits 3–0 are the phase bin 0–15, so one channel is exactly one byte. Codes 0 and 15 both give the full 8-bin width: 0 is kept as full scale for backward compatibility (向后兼容), otherwise old frames (high nibble 0) would go silent. Codes 1–14 map to widths 1–7 by integer division, (code + 1) / 2, two codes per width. 0x10 is a separate off code (关断码): the RTL turns it into width 0 (on = off) and PhaseLine holds the channel low — without that case 0x10 would decode as amplitude code 1.
Grating lobes are unavoidable because clean sampling needs d ≤ λ/2 (4.3 mm at 40 kHz). Board B's half-pitch offset cancels the 54.75° lobe.

When the primary's carrier counter reaches zero it sends a ~195 ns pulse on MISC_D to the secondary's MISC_A, once every 25 µs. The secondary samples it with its 50 MHz master clock; 5.12 MHz is divided from it by 128/1250 (ratio 9.77, not 10), removes metastability (亚稳态) with two flip-flops (触发器), then delays it by 0–255 trim (微调) steps of 20 ns (≈ 0.288° at 40 kHz) — sampling at 5.12 MHz alone cannot resolve sub-period timing. The delayed edge becomes a toggle and is re-synchronized into the 5.12 MHz domain by two more flip-flops, producing a one-cycle pulse; a toggle is used because a 20 ns pulse could be missed by the slow clock. That pulse reloads the carrier counter to SYNC_LOAD = 17, a constant that absorbs the fixed synchronizer latency

and replaces the 71 of the retired square-wave + majority-filter scheme. The 8-bit trim resets to 127 (01111111), the midpoint that gives zero phase error in simulation; trim 0 and 255 sit about +13 and −13 clocks away.
The trim command 0xE0 0x5A value is read only between frames, so a payload byte equal to 0xE0 cannot be mistaken for it.
Board select: a 0xC0 or 0xC1 byte precedes each command/frame. 0xC0 enables the primary and disables the secondary; 0xC1 does the reverse, and the disabled board ignores the payload.
Two independent UART links: primary CH340 (COM8), secondary FTDI (COM6), TX → port B, 38.4 kBaud.
Both boards play the same mode, and a parallel mode change restarts both music players, so Little Star starts together.

First verify carrier lock (载波锁定) by scoping primary MISC_D (195 ns pulse every 25 µs at counter 0) against secondary MISC_A; if it drops or jitters, the secondary stops reloading and the boards drift. Even locked, residual skew (相位偏差) leaves a static phase offset that smears the beam if trim is left at 127. Set both arrays broadside (正前方), sweep secondary trim 0–255 in steps of 8 (20 ns ≈ 0.288° per unit, so 8 units ≈ 160 ns ≈ 2.3°), and tune for the deepest null (零点) at 54.75° — null depth is far more sensitive to inter-board phase than the main-lobe (主瓣) peak. Lock that value and measure the pair at 1–3 m.

The gate chops the continuous 40 kHz drive into 4 ms on / 96 ms off (10 Hz). The mic is analysed only in the first few milliseconds after the direct arrival, before the first floor bounce.

The 54.75° null is a −25 to −30 dB cancellation. In a normal room the direct wave is followed by floor, ceiling and wall reflections; a continuous drive fills the room with reverberation, and that reflected field — even 10–20 dB below the direct — fills the null. A burst from silence measures the direct path alone.

At 3 m the first arrival is 8.75 ms after the gate edge; 0.79 ms aperture fill plus ~0.7 ms settling leave a 1.6–4.0 ms analysis window; the first floor bounce is at +5.07 ms. The 96 ms off lets the room decay ~90 dB (RT60 ≈ 70 ms at 40 kHz).

The primary outputs the gate on MISC_C (scope Ch2); the secondary follows it on MISC_F, so both boards pulse together. It does not steer or shape the beam — the frame does that; it only decides when the drive is on.

Figure 4 — Receive chain. MA40S4R piezo → battery buffer (0/+20 dB) → scope Ch1; gate on Ch2, sync check on Ch3/Ch4.
